A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 326-model study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are complete and readable, supporting reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across nine quality dimensions, including model comparisons in Table 2, correlations in Figure 4, and detailed scores in Table 12.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and the appendix experiments, including the AutoAttack comparisons in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The benchmark procedure and QUBA computation remain unchanged, including score standardization, exclusion of extreme models when estimating normalization statistics, and default dimension weights.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training-data configurations and ImageNet classification, corruption, OOD, background-replacement, and texture–shape conflict evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments in Tables 2 and 9. The complete model roster and the AutoAttack comparison in Appendix C.4 are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 2 and Appendices A and D retain the same evaluation and training settings, including attack parameters, 15 calibration bins, model-matching controls, and fine-tuning budgets.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the QUBA weighting and subsampling analyses. Appendix C retains the subgroup correlations, large-dataset OOD analysis, reproductions of prior findings, and AutoAttack sensitivity study.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same t-test thresholds and correlation p-values in Tables 2, 7, and 10. The QUBA stability analysis still uses five random samples of 100 models.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including the complete model scores in Table 12. EVA02-B/14 remains the leading model in Table 3 with a QUBA score of 1.08.

T1.justification: The QUBA definition in Equation (1) and the quality-measure equations in Appendix A are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning the nine-dimensional benchmark, training strategies, vision-language models, dataset size, and QUBA-based recommendations.

C2.justification: Scientific interpretations and qualifications are retained, including explanations of training effects and limitations concerning ImageNet generalization, proxy metrics, model-subgroup dependence, and breadth versus depth.

D1.justification: The training recipes in Appendix D, model configurations in Appendix E, and benchmark code and interactive-plot access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works. Discussions positioning the findings relative to earlier research, including the reproductions in Appendix C.3, retain their substance.

P1.justification: v3 updates author affiliations and contact information, revises funding acknowledgments and the publication header, and replaces several 'Sec.' cross-references with 'Appendix.' Scientific prose and section order are preserved.

P2.justification: The expanded author block moves the introduction to page 2 and causes text and existing displays to reflow. For example, Table 2 moves from page 6 to page 7. Scientific figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication and attribution information and clarifies appendix references, while retaining the same scientific evidence, methods, reproducibility details, and limitations. These limited editorial and layout changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
